scene: Child: (sitting and smiling, looking at the tablet)
Parent: Okay, you want to pick a story? Should we do a short story or a long story?
Child: Long.
Child: (pointing to the tablet)
Parent: Long. Okay, let's see what we got here. Okay, which one looks like a good one for you?
Child: Mine?
Child: (looking at the parent, still pointing)
Parent: Oh, or there are more books too. You want to do bad kids with stripes, that's what I'm thinking, okay.
Parent: And should we just go ahead?
Child: Yes.
Child: (turns to look at the parent)
Parent: We're ready? Okay. Ready?
Child: Ready.
Child: (looking back at the tablet, waiting in anticipation)
Parent: (getting ready to start the story on the tablet)
Child: (looking down at the tablet)

Parent: Okay. Camilla Cream loved Lima beans but she never ate them. All of her friends hated Lima beans and she wanted to fit in. Camilla always worried about what other people thought of her. Today she was fretting even more than usual, it was the first day of school and she couldn't decide what to wear. There were so many people to impress; she tried on forty-two outfits. Do you ever try on forty-two outfits?
Child: No.
Parent: No. But none seem quite right, she put on a pretty red dress and looked in the mirror, then she screamed. Her mother ran into the room and she screamed too!
Child: (looking down at hands, not paying attention to the book)
Parent: "Oh my heavens," she cried, you're completely covered with stripes!
Child: (continues looking at hands, not looking at the book)
Child: (playing with wristbands)
Parent: ...Camilla was striped from head to toe; she looked like a rainbow. Mrs. Cream felt Camilla's forehead, "Do you feel all right?" she asked.
Child: (adjusts wristbands, looking at them rather than the book)
Child: (fiddling with wristbands, still not engaged with the book)
Parent: "I feel fine," Camilla answered, "but just look at me."
Child: (finally looks up at the tablet briefly)
Child: (squirming in seat, looking away from tablet)
Parent: "You get back in bed this instant," her mother ordered, "You're not going to school today."
Child: (turns head away, disinterested)
Child: (looking away, glances around room)
Parent: Camilla was relieved; she didn't want to miss the first day of school, but she was afraid of what other kids would say and she had no idea what to wear with those crazy stripes.
Child: (scratches nose, then looks down again)
Child: (fiddling with fingers)

Parent: That afternoon, Dr. Bumble came in to examine Camilla. "Most extraordinary!" he exclaimed, "I've never seen anything like it. Are you having any coughing, sneezing, runny nose, ache, pains, chills, hot flashes, dizziness, drowsiness, shortness of breath or uncontrollable twitching?"
Child: (pauses fidgeting briefly, looks at parent)
Child: (continues to fidget)
Parent: "No," Camilla told him, "I feel fine."
Child: (glances up at parent, then looks down again)
Child: (turns to look away from the tablet)

Parent: Well then, turning to Mrs. Cream, I don't see any reason why she shouldn't go to school tomorrow. Here's some ointment that should help clear up those stripes in a few days. If it doesn't, you know where to reach me" and off he went.
Child: (continues looking away)

Parent: (points back to the tablet) The next day was a disaster; everyone at school laughed at Camilla. They called her Camilla Crayon and Night of the Living Lollipop. She tried her best to act as if everything were normal but when the class said Pledge of Allegiance, her stripes turned red, white and blue and she broke out in stars.
Child: (glances at the tablet)
Parent: That's crazy. The other kids thought this was great. One yelled out, "Let's see some purple polka dots." Sure enough, Camilla turned all purple polka dotty.
Child: (looks attentively at the tablet)
Parent: Someone else shouted, "Checkerboard," and a pattern of squares covered her skin.
Child: (leans forward, appearing engaged)
Parent: Soon everyone was calling out different shapes and colors and poor Camilla was changing faster than you can change channels on a TV.
Child: (listens attentively)
Parent: That night, Mr. Harms, the school principal called,
Child: (looks up at the parent)

Parent: "I'm sorry Mrs. Cream, I'm going to have to ask you to keep Camilla home from school; she's just too much of a distraction, and I've been getting calls from the other parents. They're afraid those stripes may be contagious."
Child: (frowns, appears concerned)
Parent: Camilla was so embarrassed. She couldn't believe that just two days ago, everyone liked her. Now nobody wanted to be in the same room with her.
Child: (nods slightly, showing understanding)
Parent: Her father tried to make her feel better. "Is there anything I can get you, Sweetheart?" he asked.
Child: (looks back at the tablet, appearing thoughtful)
Child: (Looking away from the tablet, not paying attention)
Parent: "No thank you," sighed Camilla. What she really wanted was a nice plate of Lima beans but she had been laughed at long enough for one day.
Child: (Glancing back at the tablet, slightly more interested)
Parent: "Well, yes I see," Dr. Bumble mumbled when Mr. Cream phoned the next day. "I think I'd better bring in the specialists. We'll be right over."
Child: (Looking more attentively at the tablet)

Parent: About an hour later, Dr. Bumble arrived with four people in long white coats. He introduced them to the Creams. "This is Dr. Grump, Dr. Sponge, Dr. Cricket, and Dr. Young." Then the specialists went to work on Camilla. They squeezed and jabbed and tapped and tested; it was very uncomfortable.
Child: (Focused on the tablet, following along with the story)
Parent: "Well, it's not the mumps," concluded Dr. Grump.
Child: (looking at the tablet)
Parent: "Or the measles," said Dr. Sponge.
Child: (continues looking at the tablet)
Parent: "Definitely not chicken pox," put in Dr. Cricket.
Child: (still looking at the tablet)
Parent: "Or sunburn," said Dr. Young.
Child: (looking at the tablet)
Parent: "Try these," said the specialist. Each handed her a bottle filled with different colored pills.
Child: (watching the screen intently)
Parent: "Take one of each before bed," said Dr. Grump. Then they filed out the front door followed by Dr. Bumble.
Child: (continues to watch the tablet, seemingly engaged in the story)
Child: (looking at the tablet)

Parent: (pointing at the tablet) ""Oh no." That night Camilla took her medicine. It was awful. When she woke up the next morning, she didn't feel different. Once she got dressed, her clothes didn't fit right; she looked in the mirror and there staring back at her was a giant multi-colored pill with her face in it. Dr. Bumble rushed over as soon as Mrs. Cream called. But this time instead of specialists, he brought the experts. Dr. Gourd and Dr. Melon were the finest scientific minds in the land. Once again Camilla was poked and prodded and looked at and listened to. The experts wrote down lots of numbers. Then they huddled together and whispered."
Child: (listening intently and looking at the tablet)
Parent: (continues reading) "Dr. Gourd finally spoke. "It might be a virus," he announced with authority. Suddenly, fuzzy little virus balls appeared all over Camilla."
Child: (still looking at the tablet, shows interest in the story)
Parent: (continues reading) ""Or possibly some form of bacteria," said Mr. Melon. Out popped squiggly little bacteria tails. Oh my goodness, she has tails."
Child: (looking at their knee while seated next to the parent)
Parent: Could be a fungus," added Dr. Gourd. Instantly... Are you losing interest, kiddo?
Child: No, just playing. (seated, facing sideways)
Parent: Just playing with the steam. Instantly, Camilla was covered with different colored fungus blotches. Experts looked at Camilla then looked at each other.
Child: (seated, facing sideways, feet moving)
Parent: We need to go over these numbers again back at the lab," Dr. Gourd explained. "We'll call you when we know something." But the experts didn't have a clue much less a cure.
Child: (sitting next to the parent, looking at the book)

Parent: "By now, the TV news had found out about Camilla. Reporters from every channel were outside her house telling the story of the bizarre case of the incredibly changing kid. Soon, a huge crowd was camped out on the front lawn. The Creams were swamped with all kinds of remedies from psychologists, allergists, herbalists, nutritionists, psychics, and old medicine men, a guru, and even a veterinarian. Each so-called cure only added to poor Camilla's strange appearance until it was hard to even recognize her. Is that Camilla?"
Child: (responds) "Yeah"
Parent: "Oh my goodness. She sprouted roots and berries and crystals and feathers and a long furry tail, but nothing worked."
Child: (looks slightly confused, maybe fidgeting)
Parent: "One day, a woman who called herself an environment therapist, claimed she could cure Camilla. "Close your eyes," she said, "breathe deeply, and become one with your room.""
Child: (glances away and then back at the book)
Parent: (continues reading the story)
Child: (looking to the side, with hands on lap, not looking at the tablet)

Parent: (leaning in towards the child while looking at the tablet) "I wish you hadn't said that," Camilla groaned. Slowly, she started to melt into the walls of her room. Her bed became like her mouth, her nose was a dresser, and two paintings were her eyes. Oh, there she is. The therapist screamed and ran from the house.
Child: (glancing briefly at the tablet, then looking back to the side with a neutral expression)
Parent: (continuing to read from the tablet) ""What are we going to do?" said Mrs. Cream. "It just keeps getting worse and worse." She began to sob."
Child: (still looking to the side, fidgeting slightly with hands on lap)

Parent: (still focused on the tablet) "At that moment, Mr. Cream heard a quiet little knock at the front door. He opened it and there stood an old woman who was just as plump and sweet as a strawberry."
Child: (briefly looking at the tablet again, then back to the side)

Parent: (continues reading) ""Excuse me," she said brightly, "but I think I can help." She went into Camilla's room and looked around. "My goodness," she said with a shake of her head. "What we have seen here is a bad case of the stripes, one of the worst I've seen." She pulled out a container of small green beans from her bag. "Here," she said, "these might do the trick.""
Child: (leaning on the table, looking down and not paying attention to the book)
Parent: "Are those magic beans?" asked Mrs. Cream.
Child: (continues to ignore the book and looks at their own hands)
Parent: "Oh my, no," replied the kind, old woman. "There is no such thing. These are just plain old Lima beans. I bet you'd like some, wouldn't you?" She asked Camilla.
Child: (still not paying attention to the book and playing with their hands)
Parent: Camilla wanted a big heaping plateful of Lima beans more than just about anything, but she was still afraid to admit it. "Yuck!" She said, "No one likes Lima beans, especially me."
Child: (looks up at the parent briefly, then continues to play with their hands)
Child: (sitting at the table, looking at the tablet screen)
Parent: ""Oh dear," said the old woman sadly. "I guess I was wrong about you." She put the beans back in her bag and started toward the door."
Child: (continues to look at the tablet, appears to be attentive)

Parent: "Camilla watched the old woman walk away. Those beans would taste so good, and being laughed at for eating them would be nothing compared to what she'd been going through. She finally couldn't stand it. "Wait!" She cried. "The truth is I really love Lima beans.""
Child: (still looking at the tablet, no significant change in behavior)
Parent: ""I thought so," the old woman said with a smile. She took a handful of beans and popped them into Camilla's mouth."
Child: (sitting next to the parent, seemingly engaged with the tablet)

Parent: "Hmmmm," said Camilla. Suddenly, the branches, feathers, and squiggly tails began to disappear. Then the whole room swirled around. When it stopped, there stood Camilla and everything was back to normal. "I'm cured!" She shouted.
Child: (looking intently at the tablet)
Child: (continuing to look at the tablet, engaged in the story)
Parent: "Yes," said the old woman. "I knew the real you was in there somewhere." She patted Camilla on the head. Then she went outside and vanished into the crowd.
Child: (listening carefully, maintaining focus on the tablet)
Child: (still focused on the tablet, showing interest)

Parent: Afterward, Camilla wasn't quite the same. Some of the kids at school said she was weird, but she didn't care a bit. She ate all the Lima beans she wanted, and she never had even a touch of the stripes again. I think that's the end.
Child: (continuing to be attentive, possibly showing satisfaction with the story)
Child: (looking at the tablet)
Parent: It is.
Child: (nods slightly)
Parent: It is. Okay. Should we read another one? There's more books if we swipe right. Ooooh. Okay, I think those are all the books.
Child: (frowns slightly, looking confused)
Parent: Why is it cut in half?
Child: (looking at the screen) Why? You want to read it?
Parent: (points at the screen)
Child: (looking at the parent)
Parent: "We already read it."
Child: (looks at the tablet)
Parent: "We did already read it. So, we can read it again or we can pick one we haven't read."
Child: (nods and looks at the tablet screen)
Parent: "You choose."
Child: (looking at the tablet, pointing to the screen)
Parent: (watching and listening)
Child: I choose?
Parent: (nodding) Mm-hmm (affirmative)
Child: (hesitating, looking at the options on the tablet) Um...
Parent: (still watching and engaged)
Child: I read one of these.
Child: (points at the tablet)
Parent: One of these?
Child: (points at the tablet)
Parent: One of up here.
Child: (continues to point at the tablet)
Parent: Okay, which one? One of the Dr. Suess's? The Lorax?
Child: (continues pointing at the tablet, looking enthusiastic)
Child: (looking at the tablet screen)
Parent: Yeah.
Child: (still looking at the tablet, leaning slightly closer)
Parent: Okay, excellent. (smiling and pointing at something on the tablet)
Child: (smiling, lightly touching parent's arm with hand)
Parent: I love this. (continuing to read and point at the tablet screen)
Child: (raising both arms up, holding a blue object, not looking at the tablet)
Parent: "You do?"
Child: (tilts head slightly, arms still raised, holding the blue object in both hands)
Parent: "Yeah."
Child: (starts pulling the blue object behind their head)
Parent: "I'm not really a big fan, but that's okay."
Child: (continues to stretch with the blue object behind their head)
Child: "I wish this could read to us."
Parent: (still pointing at the tablet, looking at the child)
Child: (looking at the tablet, hands moving energetically)
Parent: Yeah, that would be fancy, wouldn't it? Okay.
Child: (glancing around the room)
Parent: (pointing to the tablet, focusing on the story)
Child: (turning to look at the tablet)
Parent: At the far end of town where the Grickle-grass grows and the wind smells slow and sour when it blows.
Child: (reaches towards the tablet)
Parent: Wait, can I show this story?
Child: (smiling, looking at the parent)
